correctness.rationale: Each positive weighted zonotope vertex uniquely corresponds to an acyclic orientation. For split graph K_p∨overline K_q this is a uniformly permuted clique order and q independently chosen uniform gaps, giving exactly p!(p+1)^q distinct vertices. In endpoint-contribution coordinates X_i=t(R_i−1)+Σ_j 1_{G_j<R_i}, X_j=G_j. Uniform gap and rank covariances yield L_I=p(p+2)/12 (multiplicity q−1), L_C(t)=[p(p+1)t²+2pqt+(pq²+q(p+2))/(p+1)]/12 (p−1), L_A=(p+q)(p+2)/12 (1), and one zero from fixed coordinate sum. The two fixed eigenvalues impose κ≥L_A/L_I; strictly increasing L_C(t) crosses L_I only q≤p and crosses L_A iff q<T(p), explaining both plateau cases and an unattained zero-weight infimum. Independent full rational enumeration of all p!(p+1)^q distinct vertices in 15 small cases, up to 600 vertices, reproduced all eigenvalues. Proof is symbolic and covers every integer p,q≥2 and real t>0; t=0 cannot inherit the uniform vertex law.
